transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 16:00 PT | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Mark Reynolds (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Cygnus Head of Platforms), Sofia Martinez (CTO), Jordan Blake (Finance)

Summary (auto): Cost/units deep-dive, pilot ask, security checklist and data residency note.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
00:08 Liam: Hi Aisha, Liam here. Sofia and Jordan are on.
00:11 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Hey all.
00:13 Jordan: Jordan here.
00:15 Aisha: Awesome. Mark from our SE team is with me, he'll jump in on the perf and cost stuff. Mark, want to intro?
00:22 Mark: Yep, hi all, I'm Mark Reynolds, SE. I'll be focused on the batching, KV caching ideas and running the baseline.
00:29 Aisha: Great. Quick agenda — understand Cygnus current usage, goals, budget, and talk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and specific unit economics with batching/caching levers.
00:40 Liam: Sounds good. High level we're a mid-size wealth mgmt analytics shop. We have a few hundred internal users and some external advisor apps. We're exploring LLMs to power summaries, Q&A over docs, and an assistant. We're cost-sensitive — Jordan's watching the bill.
00:52 Jordan: yep, our budget is tight — looking to keep infra cost predictable, ideally < $10k/month to start for experiment phase.
00:58 Sofia: Also security — we need SSO, audit logs, and a KMS integration, potentially on-prem later.
01:05 Aisha: Great context. Quick qual: are you currently running anything in-prod? Or are you mostly prototyping?
01:11 Liam: Mostly prototyping with a managed API — protos against OpenAI and a small on-prem model for sensitive data. We're averaging about 1.2M tokens/day at peak dev times but expect higher if we go wide. That number is rough.
01:23 Mark: 1.2M tokens/day — good to know. For economics, important factors are sequence length, QPS pattern (bursty vs steady), and ability to batch requests or use prefix/KV cache.
01:36 Aisha: Jordan — when you said budget, is that total for all ML infra or just model API spend?
01:41 Jordan: Just model API spend. We can allocate more if the ROI is clear, but initial threshold is 10k/month.
01:47 Mark: Okay — so quick primer: Hosted is our managed API with per-token pricing; Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale; Private gives you more network control and on-prem but higher fixed costs. Key levers: batching, KV / prefix caching, quantization.
02:06 Liam: Can you walk through a concrete per-token example? The marketing pages have ranges but we need line-items.
02:12 Aisha: Sure — Mark, want to take the example?
02:15 Mark: Yep. Suppose a 512-token request; with hosted list pricing band A (example), our public per-token rate for a 512 sequence on a mid-sized model might be $0.0003 per token for generation and $0.00002 for embeddings — (note: numbers illustrative). But effective per-response cost can be reduced via batching (amortize compute across multiple prompts) and KV caching for repeated prefix. So a 512-token response at list rate ~ $0.1536, but with batching and caching you might see 30-60% reduction depending on prompt reuse.
02:51 Sofia: That per-response sounds high if we scale to thousands. Do you have examples of dedicated delta?
02:57 Mark: Dedicated reserved capacity trades fixed commit for lower unit cost. For example, a dedicated pool committed at X GPUs could reduce per-token cost to maybe $0.00015–0.0002 depending on quantization and throughput. Plus you get predictable latency. Again rough, we'll model to your workload.
03:17 Jordan: How do batching and caching actually work? Our app does a lot of short prompts that share document context.
03:23 Mark: Two levers — batching consolidates many independent requests into a single GPU pass when latency SLOs allow, lowering per-token compute overhead. KV/prefix caching stores transformer KV states for common prefixes so repeated context doesn't re-run the full forward — huge wins for chat-like flows where the beginning of conversation repeats. Both require some app changes: batching needs async request collection, caching needs stable prompt canonicalization or a cache key strategy.
03:47 Liam: Any numbers ballpark for prefix cache?
03:50 Mark: If you can cache 40–60% of tokens (prefix), you can reduce token spend proportionally for those calls — so effectively cost per effective new token drops. We'll run your sample to quantify.
03:58 Aisha: Also quantization and smaller model variants help on Dedicated — 4-bit/8-bit quantization can slash GPU memory/perf tradeoffs and lower unit costs.
04:07 Sofia: From a security standpoint, if we go Hosted, can you provide SAML SSO, SOC2, and customer-managed KMS?
04:14 Aisha: Yes — Hosted supports SSO and SOC2. For KMS we have integrations for key wrapping; for full customer-managed HSM you'd likely look at Private. We'll share our security pack.
04:24 Jordan: Data residency — some clients require EU residency. Is Hosted covering regions?
04:28 Mark: We have region routing and can pin workloads to regions. Dedicated and Private give stronger controls.
04:33 Liam: Back to cost: what about the burst model? We have spiky daily peaks with daytime trading windows.
04:39 Mark: For spiky workloads Dedicated can reserve baseline capacity and allow burst to hosted for overflow or we configure autoscaling policies and burst credits. That hybrid routing reduces commit size while keeping latency.
04:51 Sofia: Does Redwood support auto-fallback to smaller/cheaper models when capacity constrained?
04:56 Mark: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants based on a policy — e.g., reduce to a quantized or smaller model during congestion. That helps maintain availability and controls cost.
05:08 (brief silence)
05:12 Liam: Jordan's worried about the $10k monthly threshold though. Can you model an example? Say we take 1M tokens/day, mostly 64–128 token responses.
05:25 Mark: Quick mental calc: 1M tokens/day ~ 30M tokens/month. At $0.0003/token that's $9k/month purely generation — so borderline. But that's list price; with batching/caching and a modest committed tier (dedicated small pool) you can reduce to maybe $0.00012–0.00018/token effective which would be $3.6k–$5.4k/mo. We'll put together a proper model with your sample.
05:52 Jordan: That projection helps. The key is realizing the caveat: list price vs effective price after engineering effort.
06:00 Aisha: Right, and also consider SLOs — Hosted is fastest to launch but may have higher variable cost. Dedicated reduces unit cost but needs commit and ops.
06:11 Sofia: For pilot, we'd want to validate both latency and cost. Can you run a baseline with our prompts and show batching impacts?
06:17 Mark: Absolutely — if you can share sample prompts and expected concurrency, I can run a matrix: no-batching, small-batch, large-batch, prefix-cache enabled.
06:27 Liam: We'll share a week of logs and top-50 prompts.
06:30 Aisha: Thanks. On procurement, any SLA requirements?
06:33 Jordan: Not initially, just stability and predictable cost.
06:36 Aisha: Ok. A couple notes on implementation: batching may require some client-side buffering — we have helper SDKs that make it easier. Also for KV caching we'll need a canonicalization step — small engineering overhead.
06:51 Mark: Also watch out for hallucination tradeoffs when moving to smaller/quantized models; quality monitoring needs to be in the loop. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles and monitor regressions against a prompt set.
07:05 Sofia: Good point. We care about quality. Any eval frameworks you recommend?
07:09 Mark: We can run automated evals on your labeled prompts and threshold alerts; Redwood's evals tie regressions to model changes. We'll share the eval template.
07:18 Liam: If we go dedicated, what's a minimum commit?
07:21 Aisha: Typically we see commits starting at a small multi-GPU pool for a pilot — I'll include example commitment tiers in the pricing doc.
07:28 Jordan: About cost visibility — can we get token-level dashboards?
07:32 Mark: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and latency traces. Useful to spot ops optimizations.
07:40 Sofia: Any customer references in finance who ran a similar pilot?
07:44 Aisha: We can share a redacted case study — I'll attach a short one.
07:48 Liam: Great. Quick question — how does billing for Dedicated work? Is it a flat monthly commit plus overage?
07:54 Aisha: It depends on the contract; common pattern is monthly commit with some allowance and overage at an agreed rate. We'll outline options.
08:02 Jordan: Ok. Let's talk about timeline — we want to run a 4–6 week pilot if numbers look good.
08:07 Sofia: Agreed. Pilot scope: validate UX latency, cost per active user, and quality metrics.
08:13 Mark: So technical next steps: you send sample prompts + token distribution; I run baseline across batching/caching/quantization and share a spreadsheet with cost per 1M tokens under each config.
08:25 Aisha: Business next steps: I'll send pricing bands and a pilot proposal including security docs.
08:31 Liam: Sounds good. Anything else on security?
08:33 Sofia: We need SOC2 report, SSO details, and KMS integration write-up.
08:37 Aisha: We'll attach the SOC2 and SAML guide; for KMS I'll add details and note caveats for hosted vs private.
08:44 (brief cross-talk)
08:47 Liam: One more technical — can your prefix cache be persisted across requests or is it per-session?
08:52 Mark: Cache is configurable — can persist keys for a TTL and be shared across sessions if you canonicalize. For multi-tenant we recommend per-tenant keys.
09:02 Jordan: For international data residency — how fast to spin up EU region?
09:06 Aisha: We have regional hosting; spin-up is policy/config and sometimes requires a contract flag. We'll discuss timelines in the security pack.
09:14 Sofia: Perfect. Any blockers on our side?
09:17 Liam: We'll need to anonymize some of the logs before sharing. That should be fine.
09:21 Aisha: Totally. We'll treat samples as limited for the baseline.
09:25 Mark: I'll schedule an infra run once we get the prompts. Expect a 2–3 day turnaround for the initial baseline.
09:31 Aisha: Ok we'll keep that as due date. Jordan, Sofia, anything else?
09:35 Jordan: No, just keep it tight on the pricing doc so leadership can sign off.
09:40 Sofia: And include quality/regression monitoring notes.
09:43 Aisha: Will do. Recap: Redwood sends pricing bands + security docs; Mark runs perf baseline; Cygnus sends prompts. Follow-up call to review pilot scope.
09:55 Liam: Thanks everyone.
09:57 Aisha: Thanks, talk soon.
10:00 End of meeting.
